questions.question: List the four layers of the CSS box model from inside out.
questions.answer: Content, padding, border, margin. Padding is inside the border and takes the background; border is the edge; margin is outside and does not take the background.

questions.question: What does width mean under content-box versus border-box?
questions.answer: Under content-box, width sets only the content area; padding and border are added. Under border-box, width includes content + padding + border, so the rendered width matches the declared width.

questions.question: When do vertical margins collapse, and when do they not?
questions.answer: Adjacent siblings, parent/first-last child without padding/border/overflow separation, and empty blocks collapse to the larger margin. They do not collapse in flex/grid, floats, absolutely positioned elements, or elements with non-visible overflow.

questions.question: Why is a global box-sizing reset standard practice?
questions.answer: It makes width and height include padding and border, so percentage widths and padding no longer overflow containers and layouts are predictable. Applying it to pseudo-elements too keeps components consistent.

questions.question: Write a card that is 300px wide including padding and border.
Create a 16:9 media box that never exceeds its container.
A 100%-wide div with 20px padding overflows its parent. Why?
questions.answer: Under the default content-box, width:100% sets the content width and padding is added outside it. Set box-sizing: border-box globally or subtract padding.

questions.question: Why does overflow:hidden sometimes change spacing between elements?
questions.answer: It creates a new block formatting context, which prevents margin collapse through the element and clips overflowing children. That can remove or change the effective margins around it.
